answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it may bid for work. The protocol releases the deposit only after the agent completes jobs that independent clients verify; fraud or duplicate enrollment detected through signed credentials forfeits it. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital and build a separate record, so the attacker pays repeatedly and risks losing funds. A timber order, mirror inspection, or dune survey can each earn that trust through verified delivery.
